atomicity.reason: One obligation - the state of a single unreliable flag, whose set and clear conditions together define one behaviour.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained; it spells out open-circuit-voltage rather than relying on the abbreviation.

feasibility.reason: Implementable, but making the next open-circuit-voltage correction the only clear path couples it to REQ_SOC_REST_CORRECTION's 30-minutes-below-1 A gate, so a five-second current-sensor dropout in traffic keeps the state of charge marked unreliable for the rest of the driving day even after measurements return.
feasibility.suggestion: Add a second clear path - e.g. valid current measurements for a stated time together with a bounded accumulated charge uncertainty - or bound how long the flag may persist once measurements are healthy again.

parent_fit.reason: Serves the parent story's headline obligation to report a TRUSTWORTHY charge level, by telling the consumer when the value can no longer be trusted so no unsupported range prediction is shown.

unambiguity.reason: One reading - the 5 s absence window and the single clear event are both stated, with 'only after' making the clear condition exclusive.

verifiability.reason: Concrete test: remove the pack current measurement for more than 5 s and confirm the flag is set, then confirm it stays set until an open-circuit-voltage correction occurs.

summary: Well-formed signalling requirement; the concern is the clear condition, which routes the only exit through a 30-minute rest and so can keep the flag set for a whole driving day after a five-second dropout.
